questions.stem: The specific heat capacity of a substance is the amount of energy required to:

options.text: Raise the temperature of 1 kg of the substance by 1 degree C
Change the state of 1 kg of the substance

questions.explanation: Specific heat capacity (c) is the energy needed to raise the temperature of 1 kg of a substance by 1 degree C (or 1 K). It is measured in J/(kg degrees C) or J/(kg K).

questions.stem: How much energy is needed to raise the temperature of 2 kg of water (c = 4200 J/(kg degrees C)) by 5 degrees C?
questions.explanation: Using E = mc(delta T) = 2 x 4200 x 5 = 42,000 J. You multiply the mass, specific heat capacity, and temperature change together.
